s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented macules on the face and neck with a 2-year history
salient_findings: Round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
key_facts: Man in his 40s
2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions
Lesions are round, hypopigmented macules
Symmetric distribution on face and neck
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells
Glycogen accumulation in cytoplasm
Fibrous connective tissue in stroma
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Clear cell basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings of plate-like subepidermal tumor with clear/pale epithelial cells and glycogen accumulation

shortlist.label: Trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of asymptomatic hypopigmented macules and histopathologic findings of neoplastic cords

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of hypopigmented macules and symmetric distribution on face and neck

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of multiple round hypopigmented macules

shortlist.label: Trichoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings of neoplastic cords with clear/pale epithelial cells and fibrous connective tissue in stroma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple, round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, with no hair growth at the site of the lesions and a lack of response to treatment for tinea versicolor, aligns with the characteristics of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. The histopathologic findings, while not definitive, do not contradict this diagnosis and the clinical features are more typical of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis than the other options.

rejected.label: Clear cell basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While the histopathologic findings show a subepidermal tumor with clear/pale epithelial cells, the clinical presentation and lack of other typical basal cell carcinoma features make this less likely.

rejected.label: Trichoepithelioma
rejected.why: The absence of hair growth in the affected areas and the specific histopathologic findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: This condition typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented patch, which does not match the patient's multiple lesions.

rejected.label: Trichoblastoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathologic features do not align with trichoblastoma, which is a rare skin tumor.
